items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: I worked with Manuel Perez. I had an opportunity to work with him.

ctx.x: Only a few. That's what I said. Trumpet players, like Manuel Perez was a trumpet player, and they had some -- another good trumpet player, he was real light and he would pass for white and he wouldn't teach no colored at all.

Now, my teacher was Mexican. Tio, Lorenzo Tio. And his whole family was clarinet players from the great grandfather on down, the whole family. And his uncle -- we used to call him Papa Tio -- he was a better musician than his nephew, Lorenzo Tio. And he wouldn't take any -- he was a very peculiar man. If he'd take a pupil -- and the first lesson he'd give him and he could see that he wasn't going to be any good playing the clarinet, he'd tell him, "Son, I don't want your money."
